Baltimore at a glance

Since 1851 Baltimore has stood apart from any county, so city offices do work that a county government does elsewhere, from collecting taxes to keeping land records. It counted 585,708 residents in 2020, well under its 1950 peak of 949,708. Rowhouses are the dominant house type, many with brick or formstone fronts, and the city is split into nine regions that match police districts. Buyers shop by neighborhood: Federal Hill, Fells Point, Canton and Locust Point in the south, Roland Park, Hampden, Charles Village and Mount Washington in the north.

How Baltimore real property tax is billed

Bills go out every July 1. The city rate is $2.248 per $100 of assessed value, and the state rate of $0.112 per $100 appears on the same bill.

  • Payment is due when the bill arrives. Pay by July 31 and you take a one-half percent discount.
  • Interest and penalties start after October 1, at 1 percent interest plus a 1 percent penalty for every month late.
  • If you live in the house, you may split the bill in two equal payments. The second is due before January 1 and carries a small fee.
  • Filing an appeal does not pause the due date. A win means a refund with interest.

Homestead Tax Credit rules hold yearly growth in taxable value to 4% for homes their owners live in. Assessments come from the state. The January 1, 2026 reassessment lifted residential values in the city 13.4% over 2023, spread across three years.

Tax sale calendar

The city's tax sale takes place each May. A rental or other non-owner-occupied property can be pulled in at $250 owed, and a home with its owner in residence at $750.

Selling when taxes are owed

Behind on the bill? There are two clean ways out. One is paying in full by April 30, which removes the house from the sale list. The other is selling to a buyer who clears the lien at settlement, with the balance deducted from your proceeds so the title passes free.

The second route works best when you start well before the sale date. The notices in February, March and April are your warning signs. Once the May sale happens, the clock on the buyer's right to foreclose starts, and your choices narrow fast. No lender means no appraisal or underwriting, a real help against a deadline. The lien must still be paid before the deed is recorded.

Vacant and inherited houses

As of January 28, 2022, Baltimore had 15,032 vacant houses, about 13,560 of them privately owned. The number came out when the mayor ordered a 30-day review of how city agencies handle vacants, after a fire and collapse at a vacant house killed three firefighters.

The city housing department files receivership cases against neglected vacants and was on track to file nearly 500 in that fiscal year. If you own a vacant or inherited house, selling before a case is filed keeps the property out of that process. Open code notices and liens still have to be settled at closing, so pull them before you list.

Transfer and recordation costs

Expect a 1.5% city transfer tax on the consideration plus a 0.5% state transfer tax, 2% in all. Recordation tax is $5 for every $500.

Transfers are processed in person at the Abel Wolman Municipal Building, Room 1B, 200 N. Holliday Street. Document processing is open to the public on Mondays and Wednesdays only. Each turn takes up to three documents, and each deed can cover up to three properties.

What to bring to record the deed

  • Lien certificate, signed and notarized original deed, intake sheet, settlement sheet copy and the sales contract.
  • Proof that every open lien is paid. Clear them before you sign in.
  • Individual checks to the Director of Finance covering city transfer tax, recordation tax and any yield tax.

Simplifile is available if your closing agent prefers e-recording, which saves the trip downtown.

Steps from offer to closing

  1. Order a lien certificate first, to learn every open tax, water or city charge against the house.
  2. Complete the state disclosure or disclaimer form and attach it to the contract.
  3. Decide who covers transfer and recordation tax. The contract fixes the split, and the settlement sheet shows it.
  4. At the table, the closing agent pays liens and taxes from your proceeds, gathers the notarized deed and carries it to Room 1B.
  5. The deed is recorded on a Monday or Wednesday, when the office is open to the public, and ownership transfers on record.

Sellers who skip the lien certificate tend to learn about surprises on closing day. A few days of checking at the start saves a delayed settlement.

What a Baltimore seller must disclose

A seller of a house with four or fewer units must give the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer statement on or before the day the contract is signed (Maryland Real Property Code 10-702). The disclaimer says the property is sold as-is, except for known latent defects.

Sales by lenders after foreclosure, sheriff and tax sales, and fiduciary transfers from estates and trusts are exempt. If the buyer is not given the form on time, the buyer can rescind within five days after receiving it. Hand it over early and keep a signed copy, so there is no dispute later about when the buyer received it.

Can I sell a vacant Baltimore house as-is?

Yes. Maryland allows an as-is sale with a disclaimer statement, and cash buyers often prefer houses that need work. The sale does not erase anything attached to the property. Liens, tax debt and open code notices are paid or settled at closing, so a title search early in the process tells you what the final number will look like. Order it before you accept any offer.

Gather the tax bills, any city notices and the deed before you talk to buyers. Offers move faster when the paperwork is ready, and you avoid surprises at the settlement table.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Baltimore City property tax rate?

The city rate is $2.248 per $100 of assessed value, plus a $0.112 state rate on the same bill.

When are Baltimore property taxes due?

Bills are mailed July 1 and due on receipt. Interest and penalties start after October 1, and a one-half percent discount applies if you pay by July 31.

What is the Baltimore transfer tax?

The city transfer tax is 1.5% and the state transfer tax is 0.5%, a total of 2% of the consideration. Recordation tax is $5 per $500.

When does the Baltimore tax sale happen?

It is normally held in the third week of May. April 30 is the last day to pay and avoid the sale. Non-owner-occupied homes become eligible at $250 owed and owner-occupied homes at $750.

Where do I record a deed in Baltimore?

At the Abel Wolman Municipal Building, 200 N. Holliday Street, Room 1B, on Mondays and Wednesdays, or through e-recording with Simplifile. Bring the lien certificate and the notarized original deed.

Frederick housing overview

Frederick is the seat of Frederick County and the second-largest incorporated city in Maryland after Baltimore, about 46 miles west of Baltimore and roughly 50 miles north of Washington, D.C. The population was 78,171 in 2020, up from 65,239 in 2010, with 31,802 housing units and 5.8% of them vacant.

That growth means plenty of newer subdivisions on the edges and an older core downtown, where houses are far older than the rest of the stock. A downtown house can bring older wiring, plaster, small closets and stone or brick foundations. Due dates and discounts

The county mails annual and semi-annual bills in July and posts them online by July 1. Annual bills are due September 30. Semi-annual bills split into September 30 and December 31 installments. Interest starts October 1 at 1% per month on unpaid balances.

Historic district rules

If your house is inside Downtown Frederick's historic district, exterior changes need approval from the city's Historic Preservation Commission before work begins. All exterior alterations require approval unless they are on the minor rehabilitation list.

  • Sheds, fences, gates, walls and paving, including patios and driveways
  • Repair or replacement of doors and windows
  • Additions, porches, stoops, and outdoor HVAC or utility equipment
  • New lighting fixtures

Planning staff approve some projects, while larger ones go to a Commission hearing with a sign posted at the site. Call the city's Planning Department to find out whether your street is covered. Fixing up a historic house before listing can take longer than you expect, and a buyer who plans to renovate must account for the review. Selling as is skips that work for you.

Is flood risk a concern near Carroll Creek?

Parts of Frederick have a documented flood history. Carroll Creek Park began in the late 1970s as a flood control project after floods in 1972 and 1976, and it now serves as a downtown park with an amphitheater and pedestrian bridges.

Average annual precipitation is 43.52 inches, and heavy summer rain plus winter freezes can mean basement moisture, gutter problems and roof wear. MARC commuter rail runs to Washington, D.C., express bus route 991 goes to Shady Grove Metro, and TransIT runs local buses.

Do Frederick landlords need a rental license?

If you rent out your house, call the city for the present rules and ask whether any license or inspection items are open before you sign a sale contract.

  • Deferred maintenance after years of renting.

Your closing agent pays those items from your proceeds, so you do not need cash up front. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and approval, which can shorten the timeline when you are racing a deadline.

Closing day and what a cash sale skips

At settlement the title company collects the signed deed, pays the county tax balance and any liens from your proceeds, and sends you the rest. Bring photo ID, keys and any paperwork for repairs or flood insurance. Read the settlement statement before you sign and compare the tax proration with your latest bill.

A cash buyer has no lender, so there is no appraisal to fail and no loan approval to wait on. The buyer may still inspect the house and order a title search. For an older Frederick house with a long repair list, that often means a firm date and no negotiation over repair credits.

  5. Ask the title company for the closing figures, then close.

Demand is supported by Fort Detrick, the county school system and biomedical employers, but your timeline depends on the condition and price. A cash sale can shorten it because the buyer does not need lender approval.

When are Frederick County property taxes due?

Annual bills are due September 30, and semi-annual bills are due September 30 and December 31. Interest of 1% per month starts October 1 on unpaid balances.

Do I need approval to repair my house in downtown Frederick?

If the house is in the historic district, exterior work generally needs Historic Preservation Commission approval unless it is on the minor rehabilitation list. Call the city Planning Department to check your address.

The fiscal 2026 combined rate is $1.7134 per $100 of assessed value. The county-wide rate alone is $1.1100.

Most of the delay in a sale comes from paperwork, not from the buyer. Send all three on the same day and the answers tend to arrive together.

With a traditional buyer, the lender's appraisal and underwriting add weeks and can reopen the price. A cash buyer has no lender, so the closing date depends mainly on the title search and your documents. Ask for a closing date in writing, and ask who pays the transfer and recordation costs, since the contract decides that split.

  • The latest county tax bill, showing the Gaithersburg portion.

City history in brief

Gaithersburg began as a farming settlement. It was incorporated on April 5, 1878, and became a city in 1968. No. NIST sits west of I-270 on unincorporated county land. Check whether your own address is inside the city before assuming city rules apply.

Each property is reassessed every three years, with any increase spread equally across the three. You can appeal within 45 days of the notice date.
